newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt prices end higher, fresh supply absorbed.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt prices end higher, fresh supply absorbed.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices ended the Wednesday trading session higher in active dealings as fresh supply was met with good demand, traders said.
"Brady prices were higher across the board by 1/4 to 1/2 point, but Argentina was sort of a mixed bag," said a trader.
Among the notable gainers were Peruvian, Panamanian, Bulgarian and Russian debt, traders said.

"The market's been pretty firm," said Richard Segal, head of fixed income at Santandar Investments. "The tendency is for strong days to be followed by days of stability, but the bullish trend is still intact."
Meanwhile, fresh debt supply was easily absorbed by the market, traders said.
On Wednesday, Bear Stearns & Co said it underwrote a $1.28 billion of MYDFA trust certificates on behalf of the Dart family.

The Multi-Year Deposit Facility Agreement (MYDFA) certificates, which mature on September 15, 2007, were priced at 84.642 to yield 11.245 percent, or 110 basis points more than the EI Brady bond, the underwriter said.
Players said the deal was met with good demand, and the spread tightened soon after the certificates were freed to trade.
"The restructured MYDFAs tightened about 41 basis points to Treasuries," said one trader. "Pretty much everyone went short the EIs and long the MYDFAs."
The issue has a floating rate coupon that consists of Libor plus 13/16 and is similar in structure to Brazil's EI bonds, the underwriter said.
The deal securitizes all of Brazil's remaining (MYDFA) loans that had not been restructured as Brady bonds.

Among other new issues, Argentina's new global issue tightened nine basis points to U.S. Treasuries when freed to trade. However, investors flocked toward MYDFAs, which trader said were priced cheaper.
Earlier on Wednesday, Argentina priced $1.0 billion in 10-year global debt to yield 445 basis points more than U.S. Treasuries, via Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers.
The size of the deal was increased from $750 million to meet investor demand.
Still on the horizon is Brazil's $750 million global deal which is expected to come in the form of a five-year or 10-year maturity, dealers said.
In the Brady bond market, Russian Vnesh dollar-denominated paper RUVNUSLNS=RR gained 2-5/8 to end the trading day at 73-7/8 bid.
Peru Citi PEFLG91=RR debt was up 2-1/4 at 111-7/8 bid, while Panama PDIs PAPDI=RR traded up 2-3/4 to 72-7/8 bid.
In other issues, Argentine Pars AR4C23=RR ended the New York trading session up 1/4 at 59-1/2 bid, while Argentine FRBs ARFLCO5=RR were off an 1/8 at 84-1/4 bid.
Brazilian Cs BR8D14=RR were up 1/8 to 71-1/4 bid, and Brazilian Pars BR4D24=RR were up 1/4 at 60-1/4 bid.
Brazilian EIs BRFLDO6=RR were quoted unchanged at 87-3/8 bid.
Looking ahead, players are expected to focus on the release on Friday of September U.S. nonfarm payrolls and unemployment data by the Labor Department.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
